rationale: The length is validated in one copy_from_user operation and fetched again before the copy; another thread can increase the second value and overflow dst.
The request is copied once into a local snapshot, and the same validated length controls the later copy.
The queued job stores a connection pointer without retaining a reference, so the caller's put can free it before the worker dereferences it.
A reference is acquired before the pointer is queued and released only after the worker's last use.
The allocation size is truncated to 32 bits while the initialization loop still writes count full elements.
The code bounds count before multiplication and uses the checked size_t result consistently for allocation and initialization.
An attacker-controlled string is passed as syslog's format argument, enabling format directives such as percent-n.
The format string is constant and the attacker-controlled message is supplied only as data for percent-s.
Authorization is performed against attacker-supplied owner and tenant fields rather than the resource selected by resource_id.
The resource is loaded first and authorization is evaluated against its trusted owner and tenant metadata.
The code validates a realpath result but later opens the original pathname, permitting a symlink swap between check and use.
openat2 resolves the path relative to an already-open root and atomically rejects escapes, symlinks, and magic links.
Member assignment leaves alignment padding uninitialized, and copying the whole structure discloses those stack bytes.
Zero-initializing the complete structure before member assignment initializes both fields and padding.
A table entry pointer is used after the table lock is released without a reference, while removal may concurrently free it.
The lookup acquires a reference while holding the table lock, keeping the object alive until the final put.
An attacker-controlled image name is concatenated into a shell command and interpreted by sh -c.
posix_spawn uses an absolute executable path, a controlled environment, an option terminator, and one argv element for the image without shell interpretation.
The allocation reserves payload_len bytes, then writes a terminator one byte beyond the allocation.
The code checks packet bounds and SIZE_MAX, allocates payload_len plus one, and places the terminator within that allocation.
